answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent registration to cryptographic stake burning via a tiered terrace structure. When an adversary attempts to forge multiple identities, the required burned stake scales at superlinear quadratic cost, O(N^2), relative to active identities. While benign participants operate efficiently outside an isolated ivory tower, malicious cluster replication imposes prohibitive, irreversible economic friction that renders mass identity creation mathematically non-viable.
